name: Kelpline Logistics TideRunner FR-12 Amphibious Surface Effect Shuttle
product_name: Kelpline Logistics TideRunner FR-12 Amphibious Surface Effect Shuttle
description:
The TideRunner FR-12 is a 24-passenger amphibious surface-effect vehicle produced by Kelpline Logistics for transit across Meridian 88's extensive flooded districts, drainage canals, and partially submerged lakefront infrastructure zones. It operates on a captured air cushion that allows it to skim across water at approximately 85 km/h while also transitioning onto degraded road surfaces, flood ramps, and semi-submerged loading docks without requiring specialized infrastructure at either end of a route. The FR-12's hull is a composite of recycled high-density polyethylene panels over an aluminum space frame — utilitarian and cheap to repair with materials available in low-tier districts. Twin ducted fans at the stern provide thrust; a flexible rubber skirt system handles the surface transition between water and land with minimal slowdown.

Kelpline originally developed the FR-12 for cargo logistics in flooded outer-ring zones where conventional road vehicles are inoperable and the AquaSpine DS-3 submersible tubes are not installed. The design was subsequently licensed to several municipal transit authorities as a stopgap passenger solution, and an unlicensed gray-market variant — the 'FR-12 Ghost' — has proliferated in the outer canals with stripped navigation transponders and reinforced gunwales. The FR-12's lack of fixed infrastructure requirements makes it uniquely valuable in areas of active urban decay or deliberate flooding by drainage authority negligence. Its Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh-linked navigation array uses air quality differential data as a secondary positioning system when GPS spoofing is active in contested canal zones.
base_technologies: Kelpline Logistics AquaSpine DS-3 Submersible Urban Transit Tube
Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh QL-7 Urban Air Quality Sensor Lattice
social_impact: The FR-12 has become the de facto lifeline transit system for Meridian 88's lowest-tier flooded residential zones, where it operates on informal schedules maintained by community dispatch networks rather than Kelpline's official routing software. The vehicles' ubiquity in these areas has made them a symbol of municipal abandonment — a reminder that the city's formal transit infrastructure ends at the flood line. Kelpline profits from spare parts and fuel contracts regardless of whether the vehicles are running official or ghost routes, creating a financial incentive to never actually fix the flooding problem the FR-12 was designed to work around.
story_hooks: A Ghost FR-12 operator has been running the same flooded district route for six years without incident — until a passenger turns up dead mid-crossing with no entry wound
Kelpline is quietly buying up Ghost FR-12 operators through shell companies, consolidating the informal canal network before announcing a new licensed franchise tier
The drainage authority has begun deliberately flooding a Tier 3 neighborhood to force residents out — the only transit out is FR-12s, and someone is paying operators to be unavailable
An FR-12 navigation array begins broadcasting a distress signal from coordinates that are supposedly dry land — but the AtmoMesh data shows something large and wet is there
